# Review follow-up for logos eject (PRRT_kwDOVOeymc6vU0Cb).
#
# Case 1 (PRRT_kwDOVOeymc6vU0Cb): Plain Go main module directly imports logos/rt
# and logos/sync, with no .lgo support consumer. Eject must recognize support
# imports from copied Go sources, emit the shared support module, add require/replace
# in go.mod, and retain relative Go dependency replaces. The consumer build is
# the actual criterion: the ejected tree must build and run cleanly under plain Go.
#
# The platform/custom-tag scenario (PRRT_kwDOVOeymc6vU0Cj) lives in
# logos_eject_review_platform.txt.

env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Case 1: Plain Go main module with support imports and relative Go dependency
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
cd plain_support

# Native build control: logos run executes plain Go main module with logos support packages.
logos run .
stdout '^relhelp-ok:plain-support-ok:42$'
cp stdout $WORK/plain-want.txt

# Eject the plain Go module.
logos eject -o out

# The ejected Go module must build and run cleanly under plain Go.
cd out
go build ./...
go run .
cmp stdout $WORK/plain-want.txt
cd ../..

-- relhelp/go.mod --
module example.com/relhelp

go 1.27

-- relhelp/relhelp.go --
package relhelp

func Help() string {
	return "relhelp-ok"
}

-- plain_support/go.mod --
module example.com/plain

go 1.27

require example.com/relhelp v1.0.0

replace example.com/relhelp v1.0.0 => ../relhelp

-- plain_support/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/relhelp"
	"logos/rt"
	"logos/sync"
)

func main() {
	var lk sync.Locked[string]
	lk.WithLock(func(s *string) {
		*s = "plain-support-ok"
	})
	val := ""
	lk.WithLock(func(s *string) {
		val = *s
	})
	num := 42
	frozen := rt.Freeze(&num)
	fmt.Printf("%s:%s:%d\n", relhelp.Help(), val, *frozen)
}
